mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series 114i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 114i engine replacement typically costs £1,695-£2,600 for a reconditioned or rebuilt N13B16A unit supply-only. With supply and fit, expect £2,500-£3,800 depending on the specialist and location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 114i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs of N13 timing chain failure in a BMW 1 Series 114i include a rattling noise from the engine on cold start (the "death rattle"), rough idling, poor engine performance, and in later stages, the engine management light illuminating.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 1 Series 114i?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2012-2015 BMW 1 Series 114i is typically valued at £3,000-£7,000. If your 114i is worth under £4,000, a full rebuilt engine may not be economically viable - consider a used engine or scrap the car. If your car is worth £5,000+ (low mileage, M Sport spec, good condition), a reconditioned engine with warranty is a sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series 114i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 114i engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old N13 unit and fitting the replacement. Timing chain replacement alone (without full engine removal) can be completed in 1-2 days.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 114i and 116i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the BMW 114i and 116i use the same N13 family of 1.6-litre turbocharged petrol engines, but with different power outputs. The 114i produces 102 hp (75 kW), while the 116i produces 136 hp (100 kW). The underlying engine block and many components are shared, but the 116i has a different ECU map and potentially different turbo hardware.

mainEntity.name: Does a BMW 1 Series 114i rebuilt engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt BMW 1 Series 114i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers the engine against manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind when investing in a replacement N13 unit.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series 114i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 114i launched in 2011 as the entry-level petrol model in the second-generation (F20/F21) 1 Series range. It replaced the earlier 116i as the most affordable way into BMW hatchback ownership, using a turbocharged 1.6-litre four-cylinder engine that offered modest power with real-world efficiency.

milestones.description: N13B16A, 1.6L turbocharged petrol, 102 hp, launched with the F20 five-door and F21 three-door 1 Series
Production run continues; N13B16K0 variant appears in later models
BMW 114i phased out as the F20/F21 generation received its Life Cycle Impulse (LCI) update; the 114i badge was discontinued

commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series 114i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: H3: The BMW 1 Series 114i uses the turbocharged N13 engine family - a 1.6-litre four-cylinder that delivers 102 hp. While economical and pleasant around town, the N13 has a well-documented weakness: the timing chain system. Replacement demand for the BMW 114i is almost entirely driven by timing chain failure, with owners searching for "114i timing chain" and "114i engine replacement" when the tell-tale rattle appears. Every rebuilt N13 engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded timing chain components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner & Guide Failure - Why the BMW 1 Series 114i N13 Engine Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain, guides, and tensioners on BMW's N13 engine were poorly designed and constructed. The tensioner can fail, allowing the chain to become slack, which then rubs against the guides. Because the N13 is an interference engine, a stretched or snapped timing chain can cause pistons to collide with valves - resulting in catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and VANOS units
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early - rattle present but engine still running

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has snapped or engine is already damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2012-2015 BMW 1 Series 114i is currently valued at approximately £3,000-£7,000 depending on mileage and condition [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader / Parkers market observation]. This places the 114i in the "repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit" bracket for lower-value examples. If your 114i is worth under £4,000 and the engine has suffered catastrophic timing chain failure, evaluate scrap value first - replacement cost may approach or exceed the car's market value. For well-maintained, higher-spec examples (M Sport, low mileage) worth £5,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a viable investment.
problems.recommendation: If you hear the characteristic "death rattle" from the timing chain on cold start, act immediately. A £800-£1,200 specialist timing chain replacement is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild. If the chain has already snapped, the repair bill often exceeds the car's value - in that scenario, compare rebuilt engine prices through EnginesMarket against the cost of replacing the car. For owners planning to keep their 114i for 2+ years, a reconditioned N13 with upgraded timing components and warranty offers genuine peace of mind.

problems.group: Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Wear
problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Wear - N13 Engine
problems.rootCause: The N13 engine can suffer from worn valve stem seals, leading to excessive oil consumption. This is often accompanied by blue smoke on start-up and a gradual increase in oil usage between services.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve stem seals without removing cylinder head (specialist tooling)
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught before other damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new seals, guides and upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is severe and compression is low

problems.recommendation: Oil consumption of 1 litre per 1,000 miles or more warrants investigation. A specialist valve stem seal replacement using the "in-situ" method (without cylinder head removal) is often the most cost-effective solution for the BMW 1 Series 114i. If combined with timing chain wear, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components may offer better long-term value.
